Output:

28	## Components
    29	
    30	The base game has a Fall/Winter board, two battle dice, four faction boards, 54 shared-deck cards, 16 faction overviews, 4 Eyrie leaders and 2 Loyal Viziers, 3 Vagabond characters and 15 quests. There are 25 Marquise, 20 Eyrie and 10 Alliance warriors; one Vagabond pawn; 7 roosts, 6 each of sawmills, workshops and recruiters, 3 bases; 10 sympathy, 8 wood and 1 keep token; 4 ruins, 4 score markers, 3 relationship markers, 12 clearing markers and 23 items. Items are boots, swords, bags, hammers, tea, coins, crossbows and a torch. Items are not faction pieces or enemy pieces. **Faction-piece ownership cannot change**: each player owns the faction chosen in setup and its listed faction pieces, except items; possessing an item does not make it faction-owned.
    31	
    32	## Setup
    33	
    34	Use **Standard Setup**, in this order (Law 5.1):
    35	
    36	1. Choose factions; determine starting player and seating randomly. Take faction boards and their listed pieces. Use Fall or Winter. Fall has no special rules; on Winter, the river divides forests just as printed paths do. Rivers are otherwise not paths.
    37	2. Put score markers at 0.
    38	3. With two players, remove all four dominance cards. Shuffle shared deck; each player draws **three cards**.
    39	4. **Ruins and items:** Cover the four R building slots with ruins. The separate map item supply is **2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea, 2 coins**. Keep the four R-marked ruin items separate from this supply: only Vagabond faction setup hides one each of its R-marked bag, boot, hammer and sword beneath the four ruins, **one item beneath each ruin**. During that Vagabond setup, shuffle the ruin/item stacks and return each to an empty R ruin slot, keeping item identities hidden. Without a Vagabond, ruins contain no items.
    40	5. The map item supply uses its corresponding spaces near the top of the map.
    41	6. Distribute overview cards as desired; put battle dice nearby.
    42	7. Set up factions in their letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond. Setup order is distinct from turn order.
    89	- Immediate effect (paper box): resolve, then discard the **crafting card**. An item card requires the corresponding **item token** in the map supply, or it cannot be crafted. Take the item token into Crafted Items and score the VP printed on the card, subject to Eyrie exception. The item token stays; the crafting card is discarded. Ordinary factions do not exhaust crafted items as Vagabond does.
    90	
    91	| Separate component after a successful craft | Starts in | Goes to |
    92	|---|---|---|
    93	| Immediate-effect crafting card | Your hand | Shared discard pile after resolving |
    94	| Persistent-effect crafting card | Your hand | Your play area |
    95	| Item token produced by an item card | Map item supply | Crafting faction’s Crafted Items box; when Vagabond itself crafts, it may immediately take its crafted item face up into Satchel/track |
    96	
    97	- Persistent effect (stone box): keep card in your play area and gain its text, subject to the personal duplicate check above. Its card is outside your hand and cannot be spent/discarded/used for another purpose unless explicitly instructed.
    98	- **Ambush cards cannot be crafted:** the defender may play one for two immediate hits, or the attacker may play one to foil a defending ambush, matching the clearing. **Dominance cards cannot be crafted:** activate one to change victory condition, or spend it for suit.
    99	
   100	**Battle (4.3):** Choose a clearing with your warriors or pawn and an enemy there as defender. **Battle does not require you to rule the clearing.** Resolve these six steps:
   101	
   102	1. **Ambush:** Defender may play one ambush matching clearing (birds are wild). Attacker may foil it with a matching ambush. Defender's card is discarded; a foiled ambush deals no hits. Otherwise defender immediately deals two hits, then discards ambush. If no attacking warriors or pawns remain, battle ends immediately. Ambush hits are not limited by defending warriors.
   103	2. **Before-roll effects:** Resolve applicable effects; attacker chooses order if both have them.
   104	3. **Roll:** Higher die is attacker's rolled hits, lower defender's; equal dice give equal results. Each side's rolled hits are capped by its own warriors in battle. Alliance defending reverses the dice; Vagabond uses undamaged swords instead of warriors.
   105	4. **After-roll effects:** Resolve effects affecting battle that do not say “before rolling”; attacker chooses order if both have them.
   106	5. **Count hits:** Add extra hits (uncapped by warriors), subtract ignored hits. If defender has no warriors, attacker deals one extra hit for **defenseless**; Vagabond is instead defenseless if it has no undamaged swords.
   107	6. **Deal hits:** Each hit removes one opposing piece. The side taking hits chooses its own removal order, but **all its warriors must be removed before its buildings/tokens**. It also chooses order of effects triggered by its pieces' removal. Both sides deal their counted hits; losing warriors does not retroactively change the rolled cap. Whoever removes an enemy building/token scores **one VP each**, even while defending and even outside battle. Vagabond takes hits as item damage instead.
   108	
   109	Removed faction pieces normally return to supply; tracked pieces return to the **rightmost empty track space**. Placement normally takes pieces from supply, or leftmost on a track. Items removed from the game are removed permanently. Pieces are finite: no proxies. When an instruction cannot place/take/remove all prompted pieces, **you must do the maximum possible and cannot voluntarily do fewer**; this never waives costs or prerequisites, nor the Eyrie's obligation to complete Decree actions. For simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects. (1.5, G.20, G.24.)
   206	- **Move:** Exhaust one boot, plus **one extra boot** if destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction (also for forced moves). Ignore rule. **Cannot enter a forest with this action; from a forest you may move only to an adjacent clearing.** Slip has the special free-boot exception.
   207	- **Battle:** Exhaust one sword to initiate. Maximum rolled hits, attacking or defending, equals **all undamaged swords in Satchel, face up or face down**. As defender you are defenseless only with no undamaged swords. Take hits as item damage.
   244	**30 VP:** First to 30 wins immediately, on any player's turn. If multiple reach 30 simultaneously, tied player closest clockwise to current player wins, including current player. Removing enemy buildings/tokens gives one VP each regardless of phase or whether attacker/defender. Crafting items scores printed VP except Eyrie's Disdain. Faction scoring is described above. (3.1–2.)
   245	
   246	**Ordinary removal VP (3.2.1):**
   247	
   248	| Removed enemy piece | Ordinary removal VP |
   249	|---|---|
   250	| Warrior | **0 VP** |
   251	| Building | **1 VP** |
   252	| Token | **1 VP** |
   253	
   254	Faction/card scoring can add to these ordinary points. In particular, Vagabond Infamy is an **additional** point per eligible Hostile piece in battle on his own turn, except the warrior that first caused Hostile status. Do not add an ordinary removal point for a warrior.
   255	
   256	**Dominance (3.3):** In own Daylight at **at least 10 VP**, activate a dominance card from hand into play area; remove score marker and stop scoring VP. Cannot remove/replace activated card. At **start of own Birdsong**, win if ruling **three clearings of matching mouse/rabbit/fox suit**, or for **bird dominance, two diagonally opposite corner clearings**. Meeting condition earlier does not immediately win. Dominance cards cannot be crafted, but can be spent for suit. Whenever one would enter discard, put it near map available instead. During own Daylight, spend matching card to take available dominance into hand. Available **bird dominance remains bird**, so payment must be bird; a bird hand card can pay for non-bird dominance. Activation and taking are separate, neither requires a faction action allowance.
   257	
   258	**Vagabond coalition (9.2.8):** Cannot activate normal dominance win. With **four or more players**, during own Daylight at **at least 10 VP**, activate dominance to coalition with another player **not already in coalition**, whose VP is lowest among players other than you (choose among ties). **An already-activated dominance player cannot be chosen:** they have no score marker on the track (publisher clarification in **FAQ & Rulings**). Compare eligible players still on the score track. Put your score marker on partner's faction board and stop scoring. If partner wins, you also win, including if partner later activates and wins through dominance. Coalition partners are not enemies. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent. Coalition does not by itself grant Allied relationship powers.
   259	
   260	## Special Rules & Edge Cases
   261	
   262	- **Precedence:** Card overrides Law; Law overrides Learning to Play. Follow general and faction rules together when possible; if incompatible, faction rule wins. **Cannot is absolute** unless explicitly overridden. (1.1.)
   263	- **Cards:** Birds substitute for any non-bird suit, even for multiple same-suit payments. **If prompted to give or discard cards of a non-bird suit, you must treat your birds as that suit**; the instruction determines how many cards to give or discard. **Only a bird card can pay an explicit bird-card requirement; fox, rabbit and mouse cards cannot pay it.** Draw from shared deck top; when deck empties, immediately shuffle discard into new deck. (2.1.)
   264	- Hand size is public, contents private: reveal/show only if explicitly instructed. Face-up piles may be searched/inspected; deck cannot. Agreements are non-binding; cards may be transferred only as instructed; actions require no consent. (1.2–3.)
   265	- **Force:** Resolve forced actions as if affected player chose them, retaining their abilities and restrictions. A player forced to battle makes its battle decisions. (1.5.5.)
   266	- **Place/remove/replace:** Place normally from supply/leftmost track; remove normally to supply/rightmost **empty** track space, items permanently. Replace requires both removal and placement possible; the keep's placement ban cannot be bypassed by replacing an enemy piece. Swap ignores move/place restrictions. Spending a card means discarding it, with dominance's special destination. (G.5, G.20, G.23–24, G.31, G.33.)
